### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via in_flight (literal, a string literal in reapExpired))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via IHttpOutbox (symbol, a top-level interface), SqlHttpOutbox (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via INotificationOutbox (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63a9bcb773045ccffe336d0ee4876c748f5adbfb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dbc31404398cbcc414248981e4a70877b8331e72` — the merge of head `570a250c1096c8565086de20b28b0792de780773` into base `63a9bcb773045ccffe336d0ee4876c748f5adbfb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dbc31404398cbcc414248981e4a70877b8331e72 && git checkout dbc31404398cbcc414248981e4a70877b8331e72
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63a9bcb773045ccffe336d0ee4876c748f5adbfb 570a250c1096c8565086de20b28b0792de780773 && git checkout -B drift-repro 63a9bcb773045ccffe336d0ee4876c748f5adbfb && git merge --no-ff 570a250c1096c8565086de20b28b0792de780773

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63a9bcb773045ccffe336d0ee4876c748f5adbfb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63a9bcb773045ccffe336d0ee4876c748f5adbfb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `570a250c1096c8565086de20b28b0792de780773`
Local-runs: none

Face: the declaration face alone (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset at this head). There is no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path, so per `contract-review.md` the record is the lane seat's at `TIER_DEFAULT`. This corrects the claim amendment 6543085330, which named `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by analogy to #28281's triage answer; the rule sets the tier by face, and this face maps to `TIER_DEFAULT`. Inputs: card #28383 and claim 6542566200 plus amendment, the os-dev-report 6543067755, the PR's 15 files read whole at `95f4da30a`, and the one-file delta to this head (the changeset only).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`INotificationOutbox.hasDueWork?` and `IHttpOutbox.hasDueWork?` (new optional members on two exported interfaces)**: right. They are optional, so every existing outbox implementation compiles and behaves as before; the dispatchers fall back to probing every partition when a store omits them (`outbox.hasDueWork && …`). Both built-in stores (SQL and memory, each family) implement them.
- **The predicate cannot hide due work**: right. The SQL `hasDueWork` is `status: 'pending'` with `next_attempt_at` / `next_retry_at` null or ≤ now, which is `claim`'s and `claimDigest`'s predicate with the partition term and the `digest_key` arms removed: a superset. So `false` implies every partition's probe would have found nothing. The memory stores mirror it. Each dispatcher passes the same clock its claims use: the notification side passes neither, and both default to the store clock; the HTTP side passes `this.opts.now?.()` to both.
- **`DueWorkOptions` and `HttpDueWorkOptions` (two new exported types, `{ now?: number }`)**: right. Additive, no existing export changes.
- **Reap read-before-write**: not a surface change. The predicate UPDATE is unchanged and runs only when a one-row id read finds an expired claim. Expiry timing is the once-per-tick reap window #17610 already had.
- **Nothing else moves**: no route, error code, stored column, metadata key or `packages/spec` path. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/service-messaging` patch**: accepted. A non-protocol widening ships `patch` under AGENTS.md's changeset rule. The changeset at this head names the widening in one sentence.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body line `Clause-②: no`**: stale. The changeset at this head and the claim amendment are the declaration of record. The relay cannot patch the body (its first line is the attribution, not a signature), and the dev's contract leaves the body to the seat; the ACCEPT records the correction.
- **Out of scope, as dispatched**: candidates 4 (wake at the next due time) and 5 (sweep watermark), and cloud's re-measure under cloud#3413, are listed in the report. Not owed here.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-9dajyu`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QUs3BtyH9zgxKzYrJiH18J`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 通知调度器和 HTTP 调度器在 outbox 空闲时，每次轮询只读两次库：回收过期 claim 前先读一条，再用一条跨所有分区的"有没有到期行"读决定要不要逐分区探测。以前是 18 条和 10 条。
- **为什么改：** cloud 实测一个空闲租户内核每分钟读库 56 次，全是空转，这些读计入 Turso 的行读配额。
- **风险与回滚：** 有活时仍走原来的逐分区 claim/digest 路径，只多一次读；回收 UPDATE 的谓词不变，只在读到过期行时才执行。outbox 接口新增可选方法 `hasDueWork`，另导出两个选项类型（公开面加宽，Clause-② yes）；自定义 outbox 不实现它就保持旧行为。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/services/service-messaging/src/dispatcher.ts`（`runTick` 里的门）；`src/sql-outbox.ts`（`reapExpired` 与 `hasDueWork`）。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/dispatcher-idle-cost.integration.test.ts src/http-dispatcher-idle-cost.integration.test.ts`，空闲 tick 钉在 2 条 SQL。
- **需要你做的：** 无，席位落地。

席位意见：空闲开销从 28 条降到 4 条，`hasDueWork` 的谓词是 claim 谓词的超集，不会漏掉到期行；可合。

## 席位核对

- **Form:** 15 files, +407/−68. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 28403`: NOT governed, 475 lines ≤ 3000, Tier S. **Declaration of record:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, carried by the changeset at this head and claim amendment 6543085330. The PR body's line 5 still reads `Clause-②: no`; the relay cannot patch the body, and this record corrects it. `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Premise measured:** the dev re-measured on main `ac09e7b85` at the SQL client with a global `afterUpdate` hook: 18 (notification) and 10 (HTTP) statements per idle tick, matching cloud's figures; after the change, 2 and 2, against the card's bar of 6. The idle-cost integration tests pin exactly 2 statements and zero reap UPDATEs; two ablations turn the pins red. Contract review at `TIER_DEFAULT` (declaration face): 6543106545, same head, **PASS**.
- **Gates (check-runs at the pinned head):** 48 runs: 35 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. The Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check reds on `95f4da30a` were lanes cancelled when the new head was pushed, not failures; this head passes both.
- **Accepted deviations:** the due-work read spans all partitions and takes no lock, and it gates the per-partition pass instead of replacing it. Busy-path batching and digest-under-lock stay unchanged; the PR body explains the choice.
- **Out of scope and where it goes:** candidates 4 (wake at the next due time, `packages/core/src/dispatch-loop.ts`) and 5 (lifecycle sweep watermark), plus cloud's re-measure under cloud#3413, are in the os-dev-report. No card is filed here; cloud re-measures under its own card. `Skills-docs: none`.
- **Landing clause:** Tier S ordinary queue landing. The seat flips ready and enables auto-merge through the relay, then confirms MERGED and closes out #28383.
